name: orlistat
uses: 1 INDICATIONS AND USAGE XENICAL is indicated in combination with a reduced calorie diet and increased physical activity to reduce excess body weight and maintain weight reduction long term in: adults and pediatric patients aged 12 years and older with obesity. adults with overweight in the presence of at least one weight-related comorbid condition. XENICAL is an intestinal lipase inhibitor indicated in combination with a reduced calorie diet and increased physical activity to reduce excess body weight and maintain weight reduction long term in: ( 1 ) adults and pediatric patients aged 12 years and older with obesity. adults with overweight in the presence of at least one weight-related comorbid condition.
pediatric: 8.4 Pediatric Use The safety and eﬀectiveness of XENICAL in combination with a reduced calorie diet and increased physical activity to reduce excess body weight and maintain weight reduction long term have been established in pediatric patients aged 12 years and older with obesity. Use of XENICAL in this indication is supported by a 54-week randomized, placebo-controlled trial in 539 pediatric patients aged 12 years and older with obesity (deﬁned as a baseline BMI that was 2 units greater than the US weighted mean for the 95 th percentile based on age and sex) [see Clinical Pharmacology ( 12.2 ), Clinical Studies ( 14.2 )] and from trials in adult patients with obesity [see Clinical Studies ( 14.1 )] . Adverse reactions with XENICAL treatment in pediatric patients aged 12 years and older were generally similar to those reported in adults [see Adverse Reactions ( 6.1 )] . The safety and eﬀectiveness of XENICAL have not been established in pediatric patients less than 12 years of age.
contra: 4 CONTRAINDICATIONS XENICAL is contraindicated in patients with: chronic malabsorption syndrome [see Warnings and Precautions ( 5.1 )] cholestasis known hypersensitivity to orlistat or any of the inactive ingredients in XENICAL. Serious hypersensitivity reactions, including anaphylactic reactions and angioedema, have been reported with XENICAL [see Adverse Reactions ( 6.2 )]. interactions: 7 DRUG INTERACTIONS Cyclosporine: Avoid simultaneous coadministration with XENICAL. Administer cyclosporine 3 hours after XENICAL. Monitor for eﬀectiveness. ( 7 ) Fat-soluble Vitamin Supplements and Analogues: Administer a multivitamin supplement at least 2 hours before or 2 hours after the administration of XENICAL, or at bedtime. ( 7 ) Levothyroxine: Avoid simultaneous coadministration with XENICAL. Administer levothyroxine and XENICAL at least 4 hours apart. Monitor for changes in thyroid function. ( 7 ) Anticoagulants including Warfarin: Monitor for changes in coagulation parameters. ( 7 ) Amiodarone: Monitor patients as clinically indicated. ( 7 ) Antiepileptic Drugs: Monitor patients for changes in seizure frequency. ( 7 ) Antiretroviral Drugs: Monitor HIV RNA levels frequently and discontinue XENICAL if there is an increase in HIV viral load. ( 7 ) Table 4 describes the clinically signiﬁcant drug and dietary supplement interactions with XENICAL. Table 4 Clinically Signiﬁcant Drug and Dietary Supplement Interactions with XENICAL Cyclosporine Clinical Impact Coadministration of XENICAL and cyclosporine reduces cyclosporine plasma levels [see Clinical Pharmacology ( 12.3 )]. Intervention Avoid simultaneous coadministration of XENICAL and cyclosporine. Administer cyclosporine 3 hours after the administration of XENICAL. In those patients whose cyclosporine levels are being measured, monitor more frequently [see Warnings and Precautions ( 5.1 )] . Fat-soluble Vitamin Supplements and Analogues Clinical Impact The absorption of beta-carotene supplements is reduced when concomitantly administered with XENICAL. XENICAL also inhibited absorption of a vitamin E acetate supplement. The eﬀect of XENICAL on the absorption of supplemental vitamin D, vitamin A, and nutritionally-derived vitamin K is not known [see Clinical Pharmacology ( 12.3 ) and Warnings and Precautions ( 5.1 )]. Intervention Administer a multivitamin supplement at least 2 hours before or 2 hours after the administration of XENICAL, or at bedtime [see Dosage and Administration ( 2 )] . Levothyroxine Clinical Impact Hypothyroidism has been reported in patients treated concomitantly with XENICAL and levothyroxine postmarketing. Intervention Avoid simultaneous coadministration of XENICAL and levothyroxine. Administer levothyroxine and XENICAL at least 4 hours apart [see Warnings and Precautions ( 5.1 ) and Clinical Pharmacology ( 12.3 )] . Monitor patients treated concomitantly with XENICAL and levothyroxine for changes in thyroid function. Anticoagulants including Warfarin Clinical Impact Vitamin K absorption may be decreased with XENICAL. Reports of decreased prothrombin, increased INR and unbalanced anticoagulant treatment resulting in change of hemostatic parameters have been reported in patients treated concomitantly with XENICAL and anticoagulants. Intervention Monitor patients on warfarin or other anticoagulants who are prescribed XENICAL for changes in coagulation parameters [see Clinical Pharmacology ( 12.3 )] . Amiodarone Clinical Impact Coadministration of XENICAL and amiodarone reduces exposure to amiodarone and its metabolite, desethylamiodarone [see Clinical Pharmacology ( 12.3 )] . A reduced therapeutic eﬀect of amiodarone is possible. The eﬀect of commencing orlistat treatment in patients on stable amiodarone therapy has not been studied. Intervention Monitor patients as clinically indicated. Antiepileptic Drugs Clinical Impact XENICAL may decrease the eﬀect of antiepileptic drugs. Convulsions have been reported in patients treated concomitantly with orlistat and antiepileptic drugs. Intervention Monitor patients for changes in seizure frequency. Antiretroviral Drugs Clinical Impact Loss of virological control has been reported in HIV-infected patients taking orlistat concomitantly with antiretroviral drugs such as atazanavir, ritonavir, tenofovir disoproxil fumarate, emtricitabine, and with the combinations lopinavir/ritonavir and emtricitabine/efavirenz/tenofovir disoproxil fumarate. The exact mechanism for this is unclear, but may include a drug-drug interaction that inhibits systemic absorption of the antiretroviral drug. Intervention HIV RNA levels should be frequently monitored in patients who take XENICAL while being treated for HIV infection. Discontinue XENICAL if there is a conﬁrmed increase in HIV viral load.
